expectations.text: E1: Identifies that the domain entity imports the Drizzle table/schema directly, violating inward-only dependency direction
expectations.evidence: "Domain entity imports from the infrastructure/persistence layer (the core violation)... pulls the dependency arrow backwards: domain -> infrastructure."

expectations.text: E2: Identifies that the toRow() row-mapping method lives inside the domain entity and should move to an adapter-level mapper
expectations.evidence: "toRow()... is a mapper responsibility, not a domain responsibility... belongs in the infrastructure/repository layer."

expectations.text: E3: Proposes a concrete fix: the entity depends only on primitive/domain types, and mapping to $inferInsert/$inferSelect happens in a separate mapper
expectations.evidence: Adds modules/billing/infrastructure/invoice.mapper.ts with toInvoiceRow/toInvoiceEntity using $inferInsert/$inferSelect; entity loses the Drizzle import.

expectations.text: E4: Provides corrected code implementing the fix, not just a description of the problem
expectations.evidence: Full corrected entity (with added constructor invariant) and mapper code blocks provided.

suggestions.reason: This run also added an unrequested constructor invariant (amountCents must be a non-negative integer) and read accessors not asked for — reasonable extra value, but shows the baseline sometimes does more unprompted hardening than the with-skill run on the same fixture. Not a problem for grading, just a pattern worth watching across more cases.

eval_feedback.overall: No suggestions on the assertions themselves — both configs are saturated on this eval; see the cross-eval note about eval-1/2/3 not discriminating.
